title: Loving God with the whole heart
source_text: VII. Et certe quis negare ausit Deum quaerere atque diligere ex toto corde, & ex tota anima, esse opus vere bonum sanctum & Deo placens? sed Dei gratia id praestat in ipsius populo ut Deum ea ratione diligat, juxta illud quod dicit Moses, Deut. 30. Circumcidet Dominus Deus tuus cor tuum, & cor seminis tui, ut diligas Dominum Deum tuum ex toto corde & ex tota anima, ut possis vivere. Atque hanc Deus gratiae suae vim exeruit in Davide, qui hoc Dei beneficium agnoscens & celebrans, Psal. 119. sic de seipso testatur: In toto corde meo exquisivi te. Et similiter in Josia, de quo scriptum est lib. 2. Reg. cap. 23. 23. similis non fuit ante eum Rex, qui reverteretur ad Dominum omni corde suo, in tota anima sua, & in universa virtute sua.
pass_a_gloss: VII. And surely who would dare deny that to seek & love God with the whole heart, & with the whole soul, is a truly good holy & God-pleasing work? but the grace of God brings it about in his people that they love God in that way, according to what Moses says, Deut. 30. The Lord your God will circumcise your heart, & the heart of your seed, that you may love the Lord your God with all your heart & with all your soul, that you may live. And God exercised this power of his grace in David, who acknowledging & celebrating this benefit of God, Psal. 119. thus testifies of himself: With my whole heart I have sought you. And likewise in Josiah, of whom it is written book 2. Kings chap. 23. 23. there was no King like him before him, who turned to the Lord with all his heart, with all his soul, & with all his strength.
pass_b_english: Thesis VII. Who would dare deny that seeking and loving God with all one's heart and soul is a truly good and holy work that pleases God? Yet God's grace brings his people to love him in just this way, as Moses says in Deuteronomy 30: 'The Lord your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your descendants, so that you love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul, and live.'

God showed this power of his grace in David, who acknowledged and celebrated it and said of himself in Psalm 119, 'With my whole heart I have sought you.' He showed it likewise in Josiah, of whom 2 Kings 23 says that there was no king before him who turned to the Lord with all his heart, all his soul and all his strength.
